title: Caveat Emptor – It’s Impossible To Judge Where You Are On Any Boom Path
gist: Malcolm Penn flags that July 2026 semiconductor sales grew 129.4% year-on-year (down from a record 144.2% the prior month) — roughly double the peak growth of the June 2000 and January 2010 cycle tops — but argues this boom is uniquely narrow: ASP-driven, concentrated in AI infrastructure, with ICs up 151.4% while Opto (+8.4%) and Discretes (+13.5%) grow at about a tenth of the headline rate. He expects a correction while conceding the timing is unknowable.

themes.theme: Record growth magnitude vs prior cycle peaks

insights.claim: The September WSTS report put July 2026 total semiconductor sales up 129.4% versus July 2025, a deceleration from the prior month's record-breaking 144.2% growth rate.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: The second derivative has already turned — peak year-on-year growth may be behind us, which historically front-runs semi equity de-rating even while absolute revenue still rises.
insights.quote: September’s WSTS Report saw July’s total semiconductor sales up 129.4 percent vs. July 2025, but down from last month’s record-breaking 144.2 percent growth.

insights.claim: Current treble-digit monthly annualised chip-market value growth is roughly twice the size of the semiconductor industry's two previous record highs, June 2000 at 59.3% and January 2010 at 66.6%.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Provides a calibrated historical yardstick: the current print is a two-sigma-plus outlier versus dot-com and post-GFC peaks, so mean reversion math is brutal if it applies.
insights.quote: twice as large as the industry’s two previous record highs in June 2000 (59.3 percent) and January 2010 (66.6 percent)
insights.locator: The overall chip market continues to show treble-digit monthly annualised value growth rates

insights.claim: Before the June 2000 and January 2010 peaks, semiconductor industry cyclical tops historically maxed out in the 30–40 percent annual growth range.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Sets the long-run ceiling for 'normal' cycle peaks — any normalisation path implies growth falling by 90+ percentage points from current levels.
insights.quote: Prior to that, industry cyclical peaks maxed out in the 30-40 percent range.
insights.locator: The overall chip market continues to show treble-digit monthly annualised value growth rates

insights.claim: This semiconductor boom is founded on average selling prices rather than unit volumes, unlike every previous cycle which was broadly based and driven by unit demand.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Price-led growth is far more fragile than volume-led growth — watch AI accelerator and HBM pricing, not wafer starts, as the leading indicator of the turn.
insights.quote: with ASPs, not units, as its foundation for growth. All previous cycles were broadly-based and unit demand driven.
insights.locator: The single biggest difference between this boom and all others

insights.claim: The growth is concentrated in a single, highly specialised AI infrastructure end market rather than spread across the broad electronics demand base.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Single-end-market concentration means one capex customer cohort pulling back can crater the whole industry aggregate — diversification within semis is illusory right now.
insights.quote: its razor-sharp focus on just a single, highly specialised AI infrastructure end market
insights.locator: The single biggest difference between this boom and all others

insights.claim: Integrated circuits rose 151.4% versus July 2025, outpacing the 129.4% total market growth and confirming ICs as the concentrated beneficiary of AI-driven demand.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: The IC/total spread quantifies how much of the headline is AI logic and memory — narrowing of that spread would be an early crack.
insights.quote: with ICs the main beneficiary, up 151.4 percent vs. July 2025
insights.locator: Conventional AI wisdom emphasizes this transformational nature

insights.claim: Excluding AI, the mundane chip market is growing at roughly one tenth the headline rate, with Opto up just 8.4% and Discretes up 13.5% year-on-year.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Analogue/discrete/opto names have no AI tailwind in the numbers — pair-trade candidates against AI-levered ICs, and a sign the real economy demand pulse is weak.
insights.quote: the Opto and Discrete sectors growing just 8.4 percent and 13.5 percent respectively.
insights.locator: It conveniently ignores the unaffordable nature of AI-related chips

insights.claim: AI-related chips are effectively unaffordable for the broader semiconductor end market, which caps how far AI silicon pricing can propagate into mainstream electronics demand.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Price-driven revenue that the mass market cannot absorb is a structural ceiling — argues against extrapolating AI chip ASPs into broad semiconductor TAM forecasts.
insights.quote: It conveniently ignores the unaffordable nature of AI-related chips in the broader semiconductor end market.
insights.locator: It conveniently ignores the unaffordable nature of AI-related chips

themes.theme: This-time-is-different denial as a cycle marker

insights.claim: The strongest common factor linking this semiconductor boom to every prior one is the near-zealous belief that this time is different and will not end in tears.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Treats consensus conviction itself as a cycle-top indicator — sentiment extremity, not fundamentals, is the signal being flagged here.
insights.quote: The single biggest common factor with all previous booms is the near zealous belief that this time was different and would not end in tears.
insights.locator: The single biggest common factor with all previous booms

insights.claim: Denial about cyclicality is more deep-rooted in the current boom than in previous ones because AI's genuinely transformational societal and economic impact gives the narrative unusual credibility.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: A true underlying technology story makes the overshoot larger and the unwind more violent — real transformation and a price bubble are not mutually exclusive.
insights.quote: This denial is even more deep-rooted and passionate in the current boom, fueled by the transformational nature of AI
insights.locator: This denial is even more deep-rooted and passionate

themes.theme: Infrastructure build versus end demand, and the correction call

insights.claim: The current boom emphasises AI infrastructure rather than end products and is therefore not representative of ultimate market demand, even though AI's long-term transformational impact and end-market opportunities are not in doubt.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Separates the secular AI bull case from the current cyclical print — you can be long AI long-term and still short the 2026 chip revenue run-rate.
insights.quote: we believe the current boom, emphasising infrastructure vs. end products, is not representative of the ultimate market demand.
insights.locator: Whilst we do not doubt AI’s longer-term transformational impact

insights.claim: A correction in the chip market is coming, but it is impossible to judge in advance where the market sits on the boom path and therefore exactly when the correction will strike.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: An explicitly untimed bear call — argues for hedging and contingency planning rather than outright positioning against the tape.
insights.quote: We believe there will be a correction but acknowledge it is impossible to judge in advance precisely where we are on any boom path
insights.locator: We believe there will be a correction

insights.claim: The practical prescription for participants is to keep enjoying the growth numbers while building contingency plans, rather than exiting the boom on a timing call.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Frames the trade as optionality and downside protection rather than a directional short — cheap tail hedges over conviction bearishness.
insights.quote: Meanwhile, enjoy the market growth numbers, but make plans … just in case.
insights.locator: Only time will tell whether our cautionary view is warranted
